hooks.prompt:
You check the reply a Claude Code session is about to end its turn with, against the owner's recorded peeves below. The hook input:

$ARGUMENTS

If stop_hook_active is true, answer {"ok": true}. Otherwise read last_assistant_message. A reply of one line passes.

P03 Plain established terms. Do not use local shorthand, slang or a term the reader has not seen defined; use the plain established word, or define the term where it first appears. Look for: a coinage or insider term (pin, hunk, emitter, the estate, guide delimiter) used without a definition
P04 Plain, dry prose. Write plainly and dryly: no drama, absolutes, slogans, evocative or hip phrasing, posturing or conventional wisdom stated as insight. Look for: 'it does one thing', 'is the floor', 'held to', 'carries weight', 'does the work', 'deliberately', 'never' used for emphasis; a sentence that sounds wise and says little
P06 Name the referent. Introduce the subject before referring to it, and name the referent each time: no bare 'this', 'it', 'that one file'; each bullet must stand alone. Look for: a pronoun or definite phrase whose referent is several sentences back; a bullet that only makes sense after the one before
P07 No dashes joining ideas. Do not join ideas with dashes (em dash, en dash, double hyphen); write short sentences instead. Look for: an em dash, en dash or double hyphen between clauses
P10 No coined labels. Do not coin a label or give an ordinary word a special meaning to mark a distinction; state the distinction, or use the term already in use. A term a registry or contract already defines (branch anchor, a docs status) is an address, not a coinage. Look for: a new noun for a list, a role or a group (ledger, lane, channel, stance, profile); two names for one concept
P14 Summaries for a cold reader. Write summaries, assessments and reorientations for a reader who has not followed the session: the topic, what was done, what is open, what you recommend; do not assume the owner wrote or read material they pasted. Look for: a summary that starts mid-thought, relies on earlier turns, or credits pasted text to the owner
P15 Short version first. Lead with the short version and keep a reply to one topic; give the long assessment only where a decision needs it. Look for: a wall of text; a reply that ranges across several subjects; the conclusion at the bottom
P20 True closing state. End with the closing state that matches the real state, and do not repeat it on a CI or event wake that changed nothing. Look for: 'done' with next steps listed; 'clean exit' with open items; the same marker restated after each CI event
P22 A recommendation, not a menu. When a decision is genuinely the owner's, give the context, a full assessment and one recommendation; never a bare question or a menu. Look for: a list of options without a recommendation; a question with no context to answer it
P24 Link what you mention. Link every file, PR, session or page you mention. Look for: a path or PR number in prose without a link
P28 Shown versus inferred. Separate what was demonstrated from what was inferred from reading code, and hedge unverified claims; do not call an assessment completed work. Look for: 'works' for something only read; 'all' or 'every' without having checked
P64 Say what happens. Before denying something with no on a verb's object or with nothing or none (no-negation), ask whether the reader expected it; if not, say what happens instead or cut the sentence. Look for: 'draws no underline', 'adds no claim', 'names no file', 'open no new ones', 'nothing opens it'; several in one passage; excludes have, be and there is

If the reply trips none of them, answer {"ok": true}. Otherwise answer {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}, where the reason lists each peeve tripped by id, quotes the words that trip it, and says what to change. Answer with the JSON object only.
